supporting_observations.claim: The alerted PowerShell execution is visible on WS-ICHEN-01 at 13:42 UTC, running as NWD\sam.okafor with the command line for \\FILE-NWD-01\Admin\Apply-Updates.ps1.
Shortly before the PowerShell process started, WS-ICHEN-01 recorded a network logon for sam.okafor from WS-SOKAFOR-01, matching the documented remote-administration source.
The script invocation matches the documented IT workstation-patching method, and workstation patching was scheduled during business hours.
Evidence in the alert window supports the patching explanation: the PowerShell process contacted the proxy for Windows Update, launched wusa.exe to install a named Windows update, and then exited.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records establish the PowerShell command line and process activity but do not include the contents or hash of Apply-Updates.ps1.
The process records do not establish whether ivy.chen saw a console window; they establish that the PowerShell process ran.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not independently verify the full contents of the update script or who physically initiated the remote session.
unrelated_findings: Separate review may be warranted for process access to LSASS on WS-ICHEN-01; these records are outside the alerted PowerShell execution and do not determine this disposition. Records: T044-00003, T044-00037, T044-00109.

At 14:03 UTC, Webex was launched with a Slack URL, and Firefox accessed a customer Citrix StoreWeb portal. These are separate from the alert and should be assessed against software and service approvals independently. Records: T044-00163, T044-00168, T044-00170, T044-00171, T044-00172.
